mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate level, indicative of accommodative monetary policy, compresses discount rates for equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is >= 0.03 in more than 60% of 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return of SPX is positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises by more than 0.3pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%) and a stable or declining federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS change <= 0.05pp over 1 month) signals a Fed response to inflation that is insufficient to cool the economy, leading to stagflation concerns and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return of SPX is positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS change <= 0.05pp.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, strong housing starts (HOUST) and robust retail sales (RSAFS) indicate sustained consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return of SPX is negative in more than 60% of periods when the economy is in a late-cycle expansion (as defined by the NBER) and both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) relative to its 12-month moving average indicates strengthening manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is negative (<= -0.03) in more than 60% of 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts below 1000.0 thousand units signals weakening consumer demand for housing, which reduces construction activity and corporate revenue, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return of SPX is positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST falls below 1000.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer spending power and labor market health, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return of SPX is negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS and RSAFS both rise by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive policy to combat inflation, which increases discount rates and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return of SPX is positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5% and rising by more than 0.1pp.
